$comment: Single source of truth for RNIT naming conventions. Read by .githooks/rnit_naming.py, which is imported by .githooks/commit-msg and .githooks/pre-push for local feedback, and run directly as a CLI by .github/workflows/branch-naming.yml and commit-lint.yml as the real (required-status-check) gate. Also read by rnit-cli (a separate project) via `rnit_naming.py is-protected <branch>`, to decide whether a branch is a protected/base branch (no direct commits, rnit finish won't delete it) rather than hardcoding that list a second time there. Change it here, not in the scripts. branch.patterns is an ORDERED LIST tried in turn - a branch name is valid if it matches ANY one of them; this replaced the old branch.normal/branch.release two-regex shape once the approved-formats policy grew too many categories (exact names, per-base wildcards, multi-project prefixes) for two regexes to express cleanly. This is the org-wide 'approved branch name formats' policy (rollout announced separately) - the real, authoritative gate is a GitHub Ruleset configured server-side (see docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION_CHECKLIST.md, since that can't be committed as a file); these patterns exist to give the same answer locally and in CI, before a rejected push is the first anyone hears about it. The four per-base wildcard patterns (master/production/develop/staging) require a literal '-' before any suffix, not a bare '.*' - found by testing: an unconstrained '.*' let 'staging*' silently swallow 'staging_dist-anything' too, which isn't an approved format at all (staging_dist has no forward-wildcard in the policy, only its exact name and the reversed */staging_dist prefix). `protected: true` marks entries that are base/environment branches, not workable feature branches - main/master/production/develop/staging/prod_dist/staging_dist and their multi-project wildcard/prefix variants all carry it; type/<slug> and release/<...> entries don't (omitted, defaults to false).

branch.description: Approved branch name formats: exact base names (main, master, production, develop, staging, prod_dist, staging_dist), per-base wildcard suffixes for multi-project repos (master-project2, staging-qa, ...), reversed multi-project prefixes (project2/production, ...), and type/<slug> for everything else - feat/fix/hotfix/refactor/chore/docs/test allow 1-5 lowercase hyphenated words (with an optional issue-number prefix) - e.g. chore/cleanup is valid, it doesn't have to be multi-word; release/<...> is looser again, since real examples include both semver (release/1.2.0) and date-based tags (release/2025-q3).

subject.description: type(scope)?: subject - scope optional, lowercase after colon, no trailing period, <=72 chars total. Imperative mood is NOT checked here (not machine-checkable per the RNIT doc).
